1.1  Cabinet Approves Rs 30,000 Crore Additional Investment in NIIF, total commitment to Rs 60,000 Crp.6
Exam Hints:
  • What: Cabinet approved additional Rs 30000Cr in NIIF
  • Total Commitment: Rs 60,000 Cr
  • Fund Usage: Infrastructure Fund II
  • Focus: transportation, energy, digital infrastructure, urban infrastructure, e-mobility
  • Additional Funds: Additional bilateral funds – FY28-FY30 NIIF
  • What is it: India’s Sovereign Anchored Fund
  • Established in: 2015
  • Shareholder: 49% – GoI
  • Capital Commitment: Rs 40,000 Cr
Background:
  • With the fresh infusion, the Government of India’s (GoI) total commitment to NIIF has doubled to Rs. 60,000 Cr.
Investment Purpose:
  • Fund Usage: This additional investment of Rs 30,000 Cr will be used to set up NIIF’s second infrastructure focussed fund (Infrastructure Fund II), the successor to its first flagship fund.
  • Additional Funds: The government plans to launch additional bilateral and successor fund strategies during Financial Year 2027-28 (FY28)-FY30.
About NIIF:
  • NIIF: NIIF, established in 2015 is India’s Sovereign Anchored Fund, professionally run and managed by National Investment and Infrastructure Fund Limited (NIIFL).
  • Capital Managed: Government of India is a 49% shareholder, and NIIF currently manages capital commitments of about Rs 40,000 Cr across its funds and investment strategies.
  • Track Record: NIIF has a strong track record of capital deployment and has returned nearly Rs 12,000 Cr to investors through major portfolio exits.
National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) - Static GK:
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO): Sanjiv Aggarwal
Headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra
Established in: 2015

Tunnel Project in Delhi:

Greenfield Highway Corridor in UP:

1.4  Union Cabinet Approves ‘Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme’ with Rs.62,500 Crore Outlayp.10
Exam Hints:
  • What: Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved
  • Approved By: Union Cabinet
  • Ministry: MeitY
  • Budget Outlay: Rs. 62,500 crore (FY27 to FY31)
  • Replaces: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
  • Sales Incentive: 2.25%–5% (+ up to 1.5% for domestic sourcing; + 3% for Indian brands investing in design & R&D)
  • Target: Rs.39 lakh crore production, Rs.15 lakh crore exports, 60,000 direct jobs.
About Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS):
  • Implementation: MPMS will be implemented for 5 years (from Financial Year 2026-27(FY27) to FY31 and succeeds the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (PLI-LSEM), which concluded on 31 March 2026.
  • Targets: Aims to achieve Rs. 39 lakh crore cumulative mobile phone production, Rs. 15 lakh crore exports, and create around 60,000 direct jobs opportunities.
About Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (PLI-LSEM):
  • Overview: PLI-LSEM, launched in 2020, approved 32 companies and surpassed its investment, production, and export targets by February 2026.
  • Achievements: The scheme, implemented by MeitY, recorded Rs.17,519 crore in investments, Rs.11.02 lakh crore in production, Rs.6.21 lakh crore in exports, and created 1.85 lakh direct jobs.
  • Impact: The initiative helped India become the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer, with production rising to Rs.5.5 lakh crore, exports reaching Rs.2 lakh crore by FY25, and over 300 mobile manufacturing units becoming operational.

1.6  Union Cabinet Approves Bill to Strengthen Anti-Paper Leak Law with Up to 10-Year Jail and Rs 10 Crore Finep.14
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval for amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024
  • By whom: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Proposed Amendments: Individual offences- 5-10 years JailOrganised crime– 10 years Jail & Rs 10 crore Fine
  • Existing Law (2024 Act): Individual offences–3-5 years imprisonment & up to Rs 10 lakh fineOrganised crime– 5-10 years imprisonment & minimum Rs 1 crore fine.Fast-Track Courts: Special courts to complete trials within 3 monthsCoverage: Exams conducted by UPSC, SSC, NTA, NEET, JEE, CUET, railway recruitment, banking recruitment, other central government examinations.
About Amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024:
  • Key Amendments: The proposed Bill increases the minimum imprisonment for paper leak offences to 5-10 years for individuals, while retaining a maximum punishment of 10 years and raising penalties with fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised offences.Before the amendment, the Act prescribed 3–5 years’ imprisonment alongside a fine of up to Rs.10 lakh for individuals involved in unfair means and 5–10 years’ imprisonment with a minimum fine of Rs 1 crore for organised examination fraud.
  • Coverage: Act applies to public examinations conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), National Testing Agency (NTA), railway recruitment agencies, banking recruitment agencies and other Central Government authorities.
  • Fast-Track Courts: The amendments provide for dedicated fast-track courts to hear paper leak cases.
About National Testing Agency (NTA):
  • Director General (DG): Abhishek Singh
  • Headquarters: New Delhi, Delhi
  • Established: 2017

1.8  PM Family Care Tracker Pilot Project Launched in Gandhinagar, Gujarat to Strengthen Welfare Deliveryp.16
Exam Hints:
  • What Scheme: PM Family Care Tracker (PM-FCT)
  • Launched by: Amit Shah
  • Launch Date: 28 June 2026
  • Venue: Gandhinagar, Gujarat
  • Purpose: Integrated monitoring of health, nutrition, education and welfare benefits for children.
  • Coverage: From pregnancy to 18 years of age.
  • Feature: Child unique ID linked with Birth Registration Number/ABHA ID.
About the PM Family Care Tracker Project:
  • Overview: PM Family Care Tracker (PM-FCT) is an integrated digital platform for monitoring the health, nutrition, education and welfare benefits of children from pregnancy to 18 years.
  • Features: Every child will receive a unique ID linked to the Birth Registration Number (BRN) or Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID.The platform integrates birth and death registration with government databases to identify beneficiaries, generate alerts, and provide a digital Health Passport for timely welfare delivery.
  • Related Initiatives: During the launch, Health Passports were issued, polio drops were administered to children, and the first phase of PM e-Bus Sewa was inaugurated in Gandhinagar, Gujarat.
About Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA):
  • Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) is a 14-digit unique digital health ID launched in September 2021 under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).It enables individuals to securely create, store and share their digital health records with consent across healthcare providers.

1.14  Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches PRAGATI Initiative to Support 20 Lakh Farmersp.24
Exam Hints:
  • What Initiative: PRAGATI
  • Launched By: Shivraj Singh Chouhan
  • Launch Place: New Delhi, Delhi
  • Beneficiaries: 20,000 agri-entrepreneurs and 20 lakh farmers
  • Coverage: 8 States
  • Key Targets: 30% increase in farmer income; 15–20% increase in crop yield; 20% adoption of regenerative agriculture; 50% financial inclusion.
  • Supported by: PepsiCo Foundation, SBIF, Gates Foundation, IDH, Heifer International, EDF, Global Agri Entrepreneurship Academy, SAFIA, AEGF and TRIF.
Background:
  • The initiative aims to empower 20,000 agri-entrepreneurs and directly support 20 lakh smallholder farmers across India by promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.
Highlights of the PRAGATI Initiative:
  • Implementation: The programme will be implemented in Madhya Pradesh (MP), Bihar, Uttar Pradesh (UP), Assam, West Bengal (WB), Jharkhand, Maharashtra (MH), and Rajasthan, building on the existing network of 26,000+ agri-entrepreneurs supporting 26 lakh farmers.Agri-entrepreneurs will provide soil testing, mechanisation, advisory services, financial linkages and market access at the village level.
  • Targets: PRAGATI aims to increase farmers’ income by at least 30%, improve yields of major crops by 15–20%, promote regenerative agriculture among 20% of participating farmers and enable financial inclusion for 50% of associated farmers.
  • Vision: The initiative supports the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision by promoting developed agriculture, prosperous villages and higher farmers’ income.

1.16  Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Launches ‘Seafarer-First’ Initiative to Safeguard Indian Seafarersp.25
Exam Hints:
  • What: Seafarer-First initiative launched
  • Launched By: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal, MoPSW
  • Objective: Safeguard Indian seafarers amid maritime security threats
  • Regions Covered: Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz & Gulf of Oman
  • Implementing Agency: Directorate General of Shipping
  • Key Mechanism: Real-time vessel-by-vessel operational dashboard
  • Support: Medical evacuation, repatriation, compensation & 24×7 grievance support system.
Background:
  • The initiative follows attacks on the merchant vessels MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa in the Strait of Hormuz, which affected 30 Indian seafarers in the crew of 46.
About Seafarer-First Initiative:
  • Objective: To safeguard Indian seafarers through a whole-of-government response, launched after a high-level inter-ministerial review meeting in New Delhi.
  • Safety Measures: Mandates fresh threat assessments before vessel transit and directs shipowners, vessel managers, and Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (RPSL) agencies to ensure no Indian seafarer sails without adequate information, protection, and support.
  • Support: Provides medical evacuation, repatriation, compensation, welfare assistance, and a 24×7 grievance support system for affected seafarers and their families.
About Directorate General of Shipping:
  • DGS is the apex maritime authority of the Government of India (GoI) Operating under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, it oversees maritime education, seafarer welfare, and the safety and security of Indian-flagged vessels.
  • Established: 1949

  • National Library: India’s largest by collection volume, was established in 1953 under the Change of Name Act, 1948, evolving from the Imperial Library (1891) and Calcutta Public Library (1836).

  • Programme: Reform Express

  • Total Reforms: 17
  • Purpose: Modernise freight operations, improve efficiency, and enhance logistics competitiveness
Background:
  • These reforms are part of the MoR’s target to implement 52 reforms in 52 weeks to enhance efficiency, promote innovation and strengthen the railway ecosystem.
Reform 10:
  • Problem: India generates around 340 million tonnes of fly ash annually, of which nearly 96 million tonnes are utilised by the cement industry.
Reform 11:
  • Problem: Under the 4-category (I–IV) route system, where Container Train Operators (CTOs) faced separate fees of Rs. 50 crore for Category I and Rs. 10 crore for other categories, along with route-specific restrictions and varied registration requirements.
  • Reform: IR has replaced the 4-category route restrictions with a single Pan-India Container Train Operator licence with a uniform Rs. 25 crore registration fee (non-refundable) valid for 20 years, with free future extensions.
Reform 12:
  • Problem: IR, handling 85% of India’s fertiliser transport, faced operational challenges with a freight system of around 50 slabs, where entire rakes remained detained until full unloading at a single destination.

Background:
  • The new system aims to simplify regulatory approvals, promote investment, and benefit over 15 lakh Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through faster, transparent, and accountable business processes.

  • Governance: Act will be implemented through a three-tier monitoring system headed by the Chief Secretary, District Collectors, and an Executive Council chaired by the CM.

About the WTO Fisheries Subsidies Agreement:
  • Background: Adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference (MC12), Geneva, Switzerland (June 2022), the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS) is the first WTO agreement with an environmental sustainability objective and entered into force on 15 September 2025.
  • Benefit: Agreement supports traditional and small-scale fishers by regulating harmful subsidies to large industrial fishing fleets, safeguarding their livelihoods and policy space, and enhances India’s credibility as a responsible seafood exporter.
  • Domestic Framework: India’s implementation of the Agreement is supported by the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 and the Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025.Capacity building and sustainable fisheries management are strengthened through initiatives under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

1.77  India to Use Producer Price Index (PPI) for GDP Deflationp.84
Exam Hints:
  • What Index: Output PPI
  • Implemented By: MoSPI
  • Purpose: Improve GDP accuracy
  • Replaces: WPI
  • Deflation Method: Double deflation method
  • Previous Method: Single deflation method
Background:
  • PPI series was released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in June 2026 to support improved GDP measurement and align India’s national accounts with international standards.
Highlights of PPI Adoption:
  • GDP Deflation: output PPI will be used for GDP deflation to improve the accuracy of real growth measurement and reduce distortions in GDP estimates.In June 2026, WPI inflation rose to 9.87% from 9.68% in May 2026, while output PPI inflation increased to 9.57% from 9.38%.
  • Methodology Change: The revised GDP series updated the base year to 2022–23 from 2011–12 and adopted double deflation, which separately adjusts output and input prices.
  • Implementation: MoSPI plans to introduce the new PPI-based methodology with GDP estimates for the April–June quarter of 2026–27.
  • About PPI: PPI measures price changes received by producers for goods and services and is used for accurate GDP deflation.

  • India’s Count: 45 sites; ranks 6th globally, 2nd in Asia Pacific Region; 69 sites in Tentative List; UP’s 4th.
  • Criteria: Inscribed under (iii) and (vi) for Outstanding Universal Value.
  • Timeline: Tentative List (1998); Nomination (Jan 2025); ICOMOS mission (Sep 2025); Inscription (July 2026).
Background:
  • The inscription became India’s 45th World Heritage Site (WHS) and the fourth for UP after Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri.
About Sarnath’s UNESCO World Heritage Inscription:
  • Background: Sarnath was included in UNESCO’s Tentative List in 1998, and India submitted its nomination dossier in January 2025 for the 2025–26 World Heritage cycle.Following an 18-month evaluation by the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS) and approval by the World Heritage Committee, Sarnath was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
About Sarnath:
  • Ancient Names: Sarnath was historically known as Rishipatana, Isipatana (Ishipatana), and Mrigadava (Deer Park) in Buddhist literature.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites (WHS):
  • Convention: The programme operates under the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, adopted on 16 November 1972, which establishes the global framework for identifying, protecting, and preserving heritage sites.The first World Heritage List inscribed in 1978 featuring sites such as the Galápagos Islands.

6.24  India Relaxes FDI Rules for Inventory-Based E-commerce to Enhance Exports of Indian-Made Goodsp.155
Exam Hints:
  • What: India relaxed FDI rules for inventory-based e-commerce
  • By Whom: DPIIT, MoC&I
  • Objective: Boost exports of Indian-made goods.
  • Key Change: Foreign-funded platforms can now stock Indian goods strictly for export.
  • Existing Policy: Foreign investment barred inventory ownership and direct B2C sales.
  • Effective: Policy becomes effective after notification under FEMA Act 1999
Background:
  • The policy change aims to boost exports by allowing foreign-invested e-commerce platforms to procure, stock, and export Indian-made products, giving domestic manufacturers and sellers easier access to global markets.
About the FDI Policy Relaxation:
  • Previous Policy: FDI was limited strictly to Business-to-Business (B2B) e-commerce and marketplace models, strictly prohibiting foreign-funded inventory-based Business-to-Consumer (B2C) e-commerce to safeguard domestic retailers.
  • Policy Change: The updated policy permits foreign-funded entities to own inventory, purchase, warehouse, and directly export Indian-made goods to overseas consumers.
  • Implementation: The revised provisions will officially take effect once corresponding amendments are formally notified under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999, through the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019.
  • Benefits: This strategic policy shift aims to expand India’s presence in global trade and strengthen its manufacturing ecosystem.

  • Industry: Based on 5% YoY growth in the Index of Core Industries, ICRA projected the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) to grow 5–6% in June 2026.
  • Significance: The report indicates sustained economic momentum driven by industrial and infrastructure activity despite rising energy prices, supply-side constraints, and pressure on manufacturing profit margins.

  • Future Roadmap: Under Vision Mali 2063, Mali announced an Investment Forum on 3–4 December 2026 to showcase bankable projects and attract global investors.
  • About DFTP Scheme: Launched by the GoI in 2008, the DFTP Scheme provides duty-free market access to Least Developed Countries (LDCs) to promote trade and economic cooperation.

  • Framework: Three-pillar – Availability, Acceptability, & Propagation
  • Vision: Viksit Bharat@2047, One Earth One Health
  • Targets: Integration in 20 countries’ health systems by 2047Global Information Portal proposedShort-term goal (2029): 10,000 registered practitioners.
About Ayurveda:
  • Global Reach: Ayurveda exports increased from USD 1.09 billion in 2014 to USD 2.16 billion in 2023, reaching around 150 countries.
About Ayurveda Global Roadmap:
  • Implementation: The roadmap proposes integrating Ayurveda into 20 national health systems by 2047, expanding insurance coverage to 10 countries, and establishing a Global Ayurveda Register (GAR) under the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) along with international centres to strengthen global reach.
  • Phasing: The roadmap outlines short-term (up to 2029), medium-term (up to 2035), and long-term (up to 2047) milestones, including World Health Organization Good Manufacturing Practice (WHO-GMP) certification, strategic international agreements, and formal integration into multiple national health systems.
  • Establishment: NITI Aayog was established on January 1, 2015, by a Union Cabinet resolution, replacing the Planning Commission (1950–2014), and functions as a non-constitutional, non-statutory executive think tank of the Government of India.

About Geographical Indication (GI):
  • Nodal Authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI), through its Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), administers GI registrations in India via the Geographical Indications Registry.
  • Legal Framework: GI is governed by the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, administered by the Geographical Indications Registry, Chennai, Tamil Nadu (TN), which came into force on September 15, 2003 and protected under the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) of the World Trade Organization (WTO).
  • Time Period: The registration of GI is valid for a period of 10 years from date of registration and can be renewed from time to time for a period of 10 years each.

16.3  ISRO Conducts First Ground Test of SOLVE for Gaganyaan Crew Module Parachute Validation at Sriharikota, APp.303
Exam Hints:
  • What: First Ground Test of SOLVE conducted
  • Organisation: ISRO
  • Where: SDSC, Sriharikota, AP
  • Purpose: Validate Crew Module parachute deceleration system under sub-orbital flight conditions
  • Altitude: 10–17 km for Crew Module separation
  • Vehicle Features: Derived from PSLV strap-on motor, slow burn-rate propellant, straight nozzle, SITVC.
Background:
  • The test validated the solid motor for integrated parachute trials of the Gaganyaan Crew Module by using ISRO’s SOLVE, a solid motor-based test vehicle that simulates deceleration at altitudes between 10 kilometre (km) and 17 km before human spaceflight.
About Sub-Orbital Launch Vehicle for Experiments (SOLVE):
  • Objective: To test the Crew Module’s deceleration system, parachute deployment, and safe recovery under realistic mission conditions for Gaganyaan.
  • Features: It is equipped with a modified Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) strap-on motor using slow-burning solid propellant, a straight nozzle with Secondary Injection Thrust Vector Control (SITVC), and a 10-stage parachute deployment system.

  • Where: Lord’s Cricket Ground, London, United Kingdom.
  • Winner: India Women’s Cricket Team
  • Opponent: England
  • Result: India defeated England by 270 runs, dismissing them for 186 in pursuit of 457.
  • Player of the Match: Kranti Gaud
  • Key Performances
  • Kranti Gaud – 5/37 (first innings), 7 wickets in the match.
  • Yastika Bhatia – 113 (first century in a Women’s Test at Lord’s).
  • Sneh Rana – 4/42 in England’s second innings.
  • Smriti Mandhana – Fifties in both innings.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh – Half-centuries.
About India’s Historic Women’s Test Victory at Lord’s:
  • Result: India scored 285 in the first innings and 341/7 declared in the second innings to set England 457 runs (the second-highest target in Women’s Tests), before dismissing them for 170 and 186.
  • Batting: Yastika Bhatia (113) became the first woman to score a Test century at Lord’s and entered the honours board, Smriti Mandhana scored 70 and registered half-centuries in both innings, while Harmanpreet Kaur (62) and Richa Ghosh contributed valuable half-centuries.
  • Bowling: Debutant Kranti Gaud was named Player of the Match for her match-winning 7/91, including 5/37 in the first innings, the first five-wicket haul by a woman in a Test at Lord’s, while Sneh Rana (4/42), Deepti Sharma (3 wickets), and Sayali Satghare provided effective support.
  • Records: India remained unbeaten in Women’s Tests in England (3 wins, 7 draws), and the match established a Women’s Test attendance record of 37,846 across four days.

17.19  ICC Approves New Formats for Men’s ODI and T20 World Cups to Enhance Competitivenessp.333
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval for New formats for the Men’s ODI and T20 World Cups.
  • By Who: ICC
  • ODI Changes: 14 teams retained, Introduction of Round 1, New Super 7 stage, Total matches increased to 57
  • T20 Changes: 20 teams retained, 5 groups of 4 teams, Super 10 replaces Super 8, Eliminator matches introduced.
  • 2028 T20 Qualification: Scotland enters the Europe Regional Final directly, while seven teams qualify through the Global Qualifier.
ICC World Cup Format Changes:
  • ODI Format: From the 2027 ICC Men’s ODI World Cup onwards, a new four-stage format will be introduced, featuring a Preliminary Round, two groups of six teams, a Super 7 stage, and the knockout stage.The revised format will increase the total number of matches from 48 to 57, with the top three teams from each group and the best fourth-placed team advancing to the Super 7.
  • T20 Format: From the 2028 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup onwards, the tournament will begin with five groups of four teams, followed by a Super 10 stage replacing the Super 8, with the top two teams from each group progressing.Eliminators will decide the remaining semi-finalists, while the expansion of the second stage from 8 to 10 teams aims to improve competitiveness and reduce dead-rubber matches.
  • Additional Proposal: ICC approved the revised qualification pathway for the 2028 Men’s T20 World Cup and endorsed a proposed 16-team global tournament for Associate Members, subject to final approval.

  • Established: 1 July 2002, following the entry into force of the Rome Statute, adopted on 17 July 1998 by 120 nations.As of January, 2025, there are 125 state parties that have ratified or acceded to Rome Statute of the ICC, some countries have signed but not ratified it.

  • Location: The new fish species was found in the eastern region of the Lakshadweep sea, at a depth of nearly 350 to 500 metres (m) below sea level.
  • Genus Family: The newly discovered deep-sea fish species belongs to the genus Cyttopsis, a primitive group of marine fishes commonly known as ‘dories’.
  • Key Finding: Researchers from CMFRI who used Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) technology found that species previously considered to be Atlantic Cyttopsis rosea has completely distinct structures unique to the Indian Ocean.

22.3  ATREE Researchers Discover Two New Rare Solitary Bee Species in Siang Valley, ARp.408
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of Two New Rare Solitary Bee Species
  • Species: ‘Elaphropoda triangulata’ and ‘Habropoda adi’
  • By Whom: ATREE
  • Where: Siang Valley, AR
  • Published in: European Journal of Taxonomy
  • Global Count: 13 Elaphropoda species and 55 Habropoda species.
Background:
  • The findings, published in the European Journal of Taxonomy, highlight the exceptional biodiversity of the Eastern Himalayas.
About New Solitary Bee Species:
  • Species: Elaphropoda triangulata was named after its distinctive triangular abdominal markings while Habropoda adi honours the indigenous Adi community of AR.
  • Ecology: Both species are solitary ground-nesting bees that build individual nests instead of colonies, play a vital role in pollinating wild plants and agricultural crops, and are currently known only from a single male specimen each.
  • Global Significance: Globally, only 13 species of Elaphropoda and 55 species of Habropoda are known, with each newly discovered species currently represented by a single male specimen.
  • Conservation: The discovery underscores the need for surveys and stronger conservation of the Eastern Himalayan forests to protect these rare bee species from habitat loss and human-induced disturbances.

22.4  New Damselfly Species ‘Lestes paloti’ Discovered in Kerala’s Western Ghatsp.408
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of a new damselfly species
  • Species name: Lestes paloti
  • Location: Western Ghats, Kerala, India
  • Publication: International Journal of Odonatology
  • Significance: First new Lestes species from the Western Ghats in 97 years.
Background:
  • The discovery published in the International Journal of Odonatology, an internationally reputed peer-reviewed journal dedicated to research on dragonflies and damselflies.
About Lestes paloti:
  • Naming: The species was named in honour of Dr. Muhamed Jafer Palot of the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), Kozhikode, recognising his extensive contributions to Indian odonatology and documentation of Western Ghats fauna.
  • Locations: The species recorded across 6 districts in Kerala: Kannur, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Malappuram, Palakkad, and Ernakulam.
  • Habitat: Unlike most related damselflies that remain near open water, Lestes paloti prefers scrub vegetation around homesteads and laterite hillocks, often far from visible water bodies.
  • Significance: Resolved decades-long misidentification with Lestes nodalis and marked the first new Lestes species discovered in the Western Ghats in 97 years, increasing Kerala’s odonate species count to 192.

  • Hamataliwa papikonda: Recorded from Papikonda National Park, Andhra Pradesh, it is a new lynx spider of the Oxyopidae family and the first record of the genus Hamataliwa in AP.active hunter using speed, agility and spiny legs, with a hexagonal arrangement of eight eyes for precise prey tracking.
